non_blocking.finding: The watchdog rule is sound for its purpose, but it has three limits the plan does not state. (i) Subtracting the process-wide w also removes other threads' CPU waiting, including native work that runs without the GIL. A hold that overlaps at least W - 110 ms of such waiting is classed as scheduling. In a scratch probe, a 200 ms hold inside a 240 ms step with 120 ms of process runnable wait came out 'scheduling', and L1 passed. (ii) Holds up to about 100 ms beyond the 10 ms sleep are not class 2; a 105 ms between-step hold came out 'blocked'. Collections of that size are still caught by criterion 1. (iii) W - w - 10 ms is a lower bound on GIL waiting plus timer lateness plus the watchdog's own work (stack sampling, file writes), not on GIL waiting alone. The consequence is conservative: a false hold would need over 100 ms of such delay.
non_blocking.suggestion: State (i)-(iii) next to the rule and in the claim boundary, for example: a hold overlapping at least W - 110 ms of process runnable wait is classed as scheduling.

non_blocking.finding: When fewer than two watchdog wake-ups surround an interval, W is infinite. If the watchdog thread died or its log ended early, every later interval would be classed as a process-wide hold. That fails safe, but under the wrong label. In a scratch probe with the log cut at step 3,000, a later scheduling step and a ZMQ-type wait were both classed as holds.
non_blocking.suggestion: Check that the wake-up log covers the loop, up to the last step's end, and report 'watchdog log incomplete' instead of classifying.

non_blocking.finding: The check runs the unchanged evaluator on records in the live formats, and every expected class follows numerically from PLAN.md's rule. But it models an exact 10 ms watchdog cadence and takes its expectations from the rule itself. So it verifies the implementation, not the rule's behaviour on live noise. In a scratch probe with a jittered cadence (10 ms plus up to 35 ms), there were no false holds. The JSON does not record which evaluator version it ran against.
non_blocking.suggestion: Record the SHA-256 of evaluate_l1.py in synthetic_check.json, so the check is tied to the pinned judge.
